name: The Divine Council Thread
description: The Divine Council Index in its teaching order: one passage a day, with the texts that answer it.

readings.why: Let us make man in our image, and then a singular verb does the making.
God stands in the divine assembly and passes sentence on the elohim He put in charge.
The allotment that Psalm 82:8 asks God to take back. The two passages are one argument read from opposite ends.
Jesus quotes Psalm 82:6 to answer a charge of blasphemy.
Micaiah reports seeing Yahweh enthroned with the host standing to His right and left.
The sons of God present themselves and the satan comes among them.
Yahweh is feared in the council of the holy ones, and nothing in the skies compares to Him.
The throne room, the seraphim, and the plural question, who will go for us.
Thrones are set in place, plural, the court sits, and one like a son of man comes on the clouds.
Yahweh punishes the host of heaven above and the kings of earth below, then reigns before His elders.
The Most High divided the nations, and the number He divided them by is where the whole argument turns.
The end of the Song of Moses, where the Masoretic text is one line and every other witness is longer.
Israel must not worship the host of heaven, which Yahweh allotted to all the other peoples.
Babel, the scattering, and the moment the nations are set aside.
A prince of Persia resists for twenty-one days, a prince of Greece is coming, and Michael fights for Israel.
Paul tells the Areopagus that God fixed the times and the boundaries of the nations.
The nachash in the garden, and the sentence passed on it.
A guardian cherub in Eden, on the holy mountain, cast out for pride.
Helel ben-shachar, shining one, son of the dawn, falls from heaven.
The sons of God take wives, and the Nephilim are in the earth.
Angels who abandoned their proper dwelling, held in chains until judgment.
Jude quotes Enoch, the seventh from Adam, by name.
The spies report the Nephilim, the sons of Anak, and call themselves grasshoppers.
Joshua cuts off the Anakim from the hill country, and none are left except in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod.
One goat for Yahweh, one goat for Azazel, sent into the wilderness.
Legion, in Gentile territory east of the lake, begging not to be sent to the abyss.
The medium at Endor sees an elohim coming up out of the earth, and it is Samuel.
Jesus answers a charge of blasphemy by quoting Psalm 82.
Four women named in the genealogy of Jesus, each with an irregular story.
Caesarea Philippi, the gates of Hades, and the confession.
The transfiguration, six days later, on a high mountain.
Seventy sent out, and Satan falling like lightning when they return.
The struggle is not against flesh and blood but against rulers, authorities, and cosmic powers.
A woman ought to have authority on her head, because of the angels.
Christ proclaims to the spirits in prison, the ones disobedient in the days of Noah.
